title: AGI Ranker - Open AGI Score for Frontier AI Models
excerpt: AGI Ranker: rigorous open AI benchmark aggregator. 10 benchmarks distilled into one 0-100 AGI Score per frontier model. No imputation, public corrections.
content_html:
v2.0.6 · 2026-07-30 · Our social preview card was still showing pre-v2 numbers, weeks after the numbers changed. Anyone sharing a link to this site saw a card reading 14 live benchmarks, 20 models tracked and “multimodal”. The truth is 10, 21 and Visual Reasoning. The image file on our server was in fact correct and had been regenerated with the rest of the v2 release; what was wrong was our assumption that replacing a file replaces what the world sees. Social platforms cache preview images against the URL, so re-rendering the same filename changes nothing for anyone who has already shared the link, and we had verified the file rather than the card. Every preview image now lives at a versioned URL, the homepage card and all 21 model cards, which forces every platform to fetch it again. The previous files stay where they are, so an existing embed shows an old image rather than a broken one. The card generator carries the version token now, so this is a one-line change next time rather than a rediscovery. This is the same failure as the human-ceiling counts two releases ago: a rendered artifact that nobody re-derived after the thing underneath it changed. The site text was clean, and we checked: no page description, title or preview text anywhere on the site still carries the old figures.

v2.0.5 · 2026-07-29 · Tapping a specialty tab on a phone gave you a wall of text instead of scores. The specialty-index notice rendered 586px tall on a 375px screen, 72% of the viewport, and pushed the leaderboard 742px below the tab bar. A reader tapping Coding to see coding scores got a screenful of methodology and had to scroll to find a single number. Below tablet width these notices now collapse to a summary with a More expander, and the full text is one tap away in place. Collapsed, the notice is 151px and the table sits 307px from the tabs, so it is reachable in one short scroll. Nothing was deleted and nothing was softened. The visible summary is a compression, not a gentler version: it still says the specialty index is a 0 to 10 scale rather than the AGI Score, that 10 means a perfect score on every benchmark in the set, and that this is not a human-parity claim. Those are the three things a reader has to know before reading the number, so they stay visible whether or not anybody taps More. The same treatment went to the Value view note about cost being an estimate rather than a measured bill, which kept its estimate caveat in the collapsed line. Switching tabs always re-collapses, so no tab inherits the previous one's expanded state. The expander is a real button with aria-expanded, works without hover, and the Back to AGI Score control stays visible while collapsed. Desktop is unchanged: it has the room, so it shows the full text and no expander at all.

v2.0.4 · 2026-07-29 · The mobile tap states would not have rendered on an iPhone. The new section pills carry a pressed state, and it verified correctly in desktop Chromium, which is exactly the wrong place to check it. iOS Safari declines to apply the CSS active state to a link unless a touch listener exists on the element or one of its ancestors, so on the only kind of device that has a touch screen the pills would have looked inert when tapped. One empty listener on the page body fixes it for every tap target on the site. Recorded because verifying a touch behaviour in a mouse browser and calling it done is the kind of shortcut that ships a defect, and because the same trap applies to anything interactive we add from here.

v2.0.3 · 2026-07-29 · The site had no mobile navigation at all. On a phone the header rendered a wordmark and a Contribute button and nothing else. The six section links were desktop-only and the version pill was hidden below tablet width, so a visitor on a phone had no route to Corrections, Methodology or anything else, on a page that is otherwise one continuous scroll, and could not see which release they were reading. Small screens now get a compact sticky bar with the version pill visible and a scrolling row of section pills beneath it, carrying the same six anchors as the desktop nav. A row rather than a hamburger: there is no open state to get stuck, nothing to trap keyboard focus, and every section stays one tap away instead of two. Phones also get a back-to-top button once you are far enough down that scrolling back is a chore. Section anchors were landing behind the header at every width, because nothing on the page set a scroll margin; jumping to Corrections put its own heading underneath the sticky bar. Fixed for both layouts. Nothing else moved: the desktop bar is unchanged, and no score, weight or benchmark is touched by this release.

v2.0.2 · 2026-07-29 · We were overstating how much of the scale is anchored to humans. Three places on this site claimed that three or four scored benchmarks carry a measured human ceiling, and named OSWorld, FrontierMath and SimpleBench among them. The correct number is one. Of the ten benchmarks on the board, only GPQA Diamond (0.81) carries a measured human ceiling; the other nine are scored against the benchmark maximum, where 100 means a perfect score and no human claim is made at all. The other three did pass the same ceiling audit, and none of them is on the board: OSWorld (0.72) was retired in this very release, and FrontierMath (0.35) and SimpleBench (0.837) have no harvested coverage yet. The claim was wrong in the AGI definition modal, in the methodology summary and in the full methodology, and the three did not even agree with one another. This is the same class of error as the correction we published two versions ago: a number that survived because nobody re-derived it after the thing underneath it changed. The AGI Score is a mixed scale, and it is a good deal more mixed than we were saying. Also in this release: the DeepSeek apology is signed by Barak Laniado, founder and CEO, and its corrections contact is now an email address you can actually write to rather than a link back into the site. The calibration constants box no longer reads “Current as of v1.4” under a v2 banner; the constants are unchanged and were re-confirmed for v2.0.0, which is what it now says. Three hover styles on the corrections card and twelve layout classes on the apology page were also missing from the compiled stylesheet, which is purged to what the leaderboard uses, so they had been failing silently.

v2.0.1 · 2026-07-29 · The DeepSeek apology gets its own page. The correction we published in v2.0.0, an ARC-AGI-2 score attributed to DeepSeek V4 Pro that carried no source at all, now has a dedicated page at /corrections/deepseek-arc-agi-2, linked from its entry in the log above. An apology buried as one card among several is easy to walk past, and this one should be readable, citable and linkable on its own. The page sets out what we published, why it was wrong, what it did and did not affect, and what changed in the process so that it cannot recur: under methodology v2 a recorded source is a condition of scoring rather than an expectation, and all 156 scored cells carry one. The wording of the apology itself is unchanged and identical in both places. One count in that entry was also wrong. It said three further cells were voided in the same pass and then referred to four of them in the next sentence. Four further cells were voided, five in total including the DeepSeek one. Corrected here rather than quietly.

v2.0.0 · 2026-07-29 · Methodology v2. Every score falls, and no model got worse. Two changes drive it. First, human ceilings. Because a score is normalised as raw divided by a human ceiling, that ceiling is not only an anchor for what counts as human level, it is a volume knob: it multiplies both the level and the spread of a benchmark, and so how hard that benchmark pushes on its component. Most of ours had no measurement behind them. Humanity’s Last Exam sat at 0.50, a number our own internal audit described as a policy floor rather than a finding, and that setting quietly made HLE count double. From now on a ceiling is either a published human result under a protocol comparable to the models’, or it is simply the benchmark maximum and we make no human claim at all. Only four survived the test: GPQA Diamond at 0.81, OSWorld at 0.72 (which we raised, having carried 0.85 against our own recorded measurement), FrontierMath at 0.35, and SimpleBench at 0.837, where we had rounded a human baseline up. Eleven moved to 1.00. Three component scores that previously sat above 100, on a scale whose 100 is meant to be the human mark, no longer do. Second, Agency was rebuilt on four legs across three independent evaluators: SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, τ³-Banking and LiveBench Agentic Coding. Terminal-Bench now comes from vals.ai rather than Artificial Analysis, cutting our reliance on any single evaluator. τ³-Banking enters at benchmark maximum, so its true range shows: the best model completes about a third of these stateful banking workflows. Retired: SWE-bench Pro, OSWorld, BrowseComp, Tau-bench retail and airline, Aider Polyglot, Terminal-Bench 2.0. MCP Atlas demoted to informational. The Tool Use tab is withdrawn until a second clean non-coding benchmark exists. Scores fell by about 6 points from the ceiling change and further from the Agency rebuild; ordering shifted only locally, and the top two are unchanged. Third, evaluator concentration. Artificial Analysis had been supplying 45% of the whole board, 97% of Knowledge and 100% of Visual Reasoning, so one evaluator changing terms would have taken two components to zero. GPQA Diamond and MMMU-Pro moved to vals.ai alongside Terminal-Bench 2.1, taking Artificial Analysis to 26% of the board and splitting Knowledge 52/48 between two evaluators. Every switch was measured before it was made rather than after, and each offset is published rather than absorbed: GPQA Diamond −0.30pp with 1.38pp scatter across all 20 models, MMMU-Pro +5.71pp with 1.67pp scatter and vals higher on all eleven comparable models, Terminal-Bench 2.1 −7.77pp with 4.54pp scatter and vals lower on 18 of 19. One row is held rather than used: vals reports Grok 4.5 at 61.8 on MMMU-Pro, below Grok 4.3 at 83.1 and below xAI’s own non-reasoning variants, which is not a capability measurement we can account for, so we do not use it. Grok 4.5 consequently has no Visual Reasoning cell and falls three places. Visual Reasoning is still single-source, having moved from wholly Artificial Analysis to wholly vals.ai: it rests on one benchmark, so this relocates the dependency rather than removing it, and we would rather say so than imply it is solved. Also in this release: the Reasoning specialty tab is withdrawn. It ran on ARC-AGI-2 and AIME 2025, but AIME 2025 is scored for a single model and sits at 98-99% where it appears, so the tab was ranking on ARC-AGI-2 alone while labelled as using two benchmarks. Withdrawn under the same rule as Tool Use rather than kept with a misleading label; it returns when AIME 2026 is harvested. Cursor Composer 2.5 is removed from the board: it is a product system rather than a model, so under v2 it scores no cells at all, and listing it implied we were waiting on evidence that was never coming. Specialty tabs now report a 0 to 10 index rather than a 0 to 100 score. On the AGI Score, 100 means the genesis of AGI; a specialty score never meant that, and showing both on the same scale implied they were the same kind of claim. Ten now means a perfect score on every benchmark in that set, with no human comparison implied, because most of those benchmarks have no published human study to compare against. The Multimodal component is renamed Visual Reasoning. It rests on a single scored benchmark, MMMU-Pro, which is an exam built on diagrams and charts, so calling 11% of the score “multimodal” claimed a breadth of perception we do not measure. Visual Reasoning says what it is: interpreting image data, which underpins reading a chart, extracting a figure from a document, or working from a screenshot. The AGI definition was revised in the same pass and for the same reason. It previously excluded “sensory perceptions whatsoever”, which contradicted our own scoring of a diagram-based benchmark. Rather than bolt vision on, which would have raised the obvious question of why sight and not hearing or smell, we removed the sensory clause and let the physical-body clause carry the weight: what reaches a model as data is in scope, what needs a body to acquire is not. The definition got shorter. The corrections summary counters have also been replaced. They had been hardcoded since May and one of them read “1 model entered scoring” for two months without meaning anything; they are now derived from the scoring ledger on every release.

v1.11.28 · 2026-07-25 · Corrections to our corrections. We audited this log against our own commit history and found that two entries were wrong. Both times we compared two different configurations of the same benchmark and reported the difference as a laboratory overstating its results. DeepSeek did not overstate GPQA Diamond: the 72.9% we published as an independent contradiction is DeepSeek’s own non-thinking-mode figure, reaching us through a secondary aggregator and set against their thinking-mode result. Measured like for like, their self-report sits 1.3 points above independent measurement rather than 17.2 points above. Moonshot did not overstate Humanity’s Last Exam: their 54.0% was explicitly labelled as a with-tools result, and the same post published 36.4% without tools, within half a point of independent measurement. Our source policy had excluded them on the strength of that misreading. Both entries are retracted and both originals are retained rather than deleted. We have also withdrawn a laboratory promotion test that the policy described but that was never run, and corrected an entry which presented source relabelling as new independent measurement. No score, weight, human ceiling or source tier changed in this release.

Added Claude Opus 5 on five independent, variant-distinct frozen-v1 cells: ARC-AGI-2 90.4%, SWE-bench Verified 97.0%, HLE 52.59%, GPQA Diamond 93.23%, and MMMU-Pro 84.74%. The unchanged eligibility engine places it Provisional at 97.31 because one Agency cell and no accepted LiveBench row leave two thin components. The available LiveBench EAP row remains held pending public-model identity resolution; Terminal-Bench 2.1, ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-3 remain outside frozen-v1 scoring. Anthropic’s active latest-two roster is now Opus 5 and Opus 4.8. Fable 5 leaves the current roster under an identity-integrity exception because fallback-enabled, fallback-disabled and generic rows cannot be combined into one standalone model; Opus 4.7 thinking and base retire as older generations. All historical evidence remains preserved, with no transfer or imputation. No formula, weight or source tier changed.

High is the single frozen-v1 scoring configuration; the equal-scoring Medium result and the Low result remain supporting provenance only. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-3 remain informational, and no formula, weight, source tier, roster entry or unrelated evidence changed. No imputation.

v1.11.25 · 2026-07-22 · Capability Heatmap isolated from custom weights. The heatmap now reads a separately stored canonical snapshot of default-weight AGI Score, component values, coverage and tier. Explorer sliders and presets continue to recompute AI Score and leaderboard order without changing any heatmap value, order, colour, tooltip or accessible label. This fixes the state-dependent path left open by v1.11.24, whose direct score accessor still pointed to mutable custom-weight state. No score, rank, component, benchmark, evidence, eligibility or methodology changed. No imputation.

v1.11.24 · 2026-07-22 · Capability Heatmap AGI Score binding locked. The rightmost heatmap column now declares its full-precision value, colour and accessible label directly from the same canonical final score field used by the leaderboard, model details and Explorer; its default order is explicitly canonical AGI Score descending. A no-cache v1.11.23 preflight already rendered the canonical values, so this release changes no score, rank, component, benchmark, evidence, eligibility or methodology. It adds a machine-verifiable binding contract and rendered-DOM regression coverage against an Agency-column regression.

The unchanged eligibility engine places Inkling Ranked #17 at 70.97; it remains Coding-ineligible at 1/3 because SWE-bench Pro and Terminal-Bench 2.0 are absent. Terminal-Bench 2.1 remains held as a distinct version, and ARC-AGI-2 remains missing. No formula, weight, source tier, roster, or existing K3 cell changed. No imputation.

v1.11.20 · 2026-07-14 · Visual Identity Patch. Added official model-family and provider marks across AGI Ranker’s model surfaces, with local assets, accessible fallbacks and no scoring changes.

v1.11.18 · 2026-07-12 · Muse Spark 1.1 and Sol pricing. Added official GPT-5.6 Sol API pricing of $5 input, $0.50 cached input, and $30 output per million tokens. No benchmark methodology or weights changed. No imputation.

v1.11.17 · 2026-07-10 · Composer benchmark identity corrected. Composer remains Coding-eligible through SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench. No other Coding score values change, though ranks #4–#9 shift down one position. The removed evidence is retained internally for future Coding Systems consideration. The Ranked AGI leaderboard is unchanged. No imputation.

v1.11.16 · 2026-07-09 · GPT-5.6 Sol added. Added GPT-5.6 Sol from six screenshot-confirmed current-schema cells: ARC-AGI-2, GPQA Diamond, HLE, LiveBench, MMMU-Pro and SWE-bench Verified. With Sol now Ranked, the GPT-5.4 family was retired under AGI Ranker’s latest-two-OpenAI-generations roster rule. GPT-5.6 Terra/Luna and Muse Spark 1.1 were not added pending separate scoreable coverage. AA Intelligence Index remains informational and unscored.

So far only the lab's own launch-day numbers are public (its model card and a benchmark aggregator relaying the same figures), which we exclude as unverified self-reports. v1.11.5 · 2026-06-16 · Hero badge. The launch-month pill now reads "Since May 2026" - a founding mark rather than a stale-looking date stamp. No scoring change.

v1.11.4 · 2026-06-16 · Count consistency. The hero subhead and structured data still read "15 benchmarks" after yesterday's removal of the AA Index; both now read 14, matching the live count. No scoring change.

v1.11.3 · 2026-06-16 · AA Intelligence Index removed from the score. Artificial Analysis shipped Intelligence Index v4.1, an explicitly agentic composite (GDPval, Terminal-Bench 2.1, τ³-Banking, SciCode, HLE, GPQA and more). Because it re-bundles benchmarks we already score directly, keeping it as our Language signal would double-count those results and mislabel agency as language - so we removed it from the AGI Score (14 live benchmarks now). Language rests on LiveBench; a dedicated language benchmark is on the roadmap. Most scores rise ~0.3-0.5 (the Index had been a slight drag); the ranking is unchanged. We still track the AA Index as an external reference.

v1.11.2 · 2026-06-16 · Cleaner number type. Scores and stats now render in Inter with tabular figures - more legible in the dense tables than the previous display face, and consistent across the site. Headings and the wordmark are unchanged. No change to any score.

v1.11.1 · 2026-06-16 · Value view polish. Refined the value-for-money UI and method after testing: the ranking now leads with the picks (Top / Best value / Budget) instead of a raw value index that was hard to read at a glance, the cost column is labelled $/1M tokens for clarity, and the methodology page now spells out exactly how value for money is derived. No change to any score.

v1.11.0 · 2026-06-15 · Value view. The Value tab ranks models by capability against an estimated API cost. Pick a capability area - Overall (the AGI Score) or Coding, Reasoning, Knowledge, Tool Use - and the table shows the exact same score that area's own tab shows, next to an estimated cost at that area's typical token mix (cache-aware). Sort by capability or by value for money, and read the picks at a glance: top capability, best value, and budget. A value-frontier graph plots the same models. Also renamed Google to Google DeepMind, and renamed the Agentic specialty to Tool Use (coding is also agentic, so the old name was ambiguous; Tool Use covers computer use, web browsing and tool/function calling beyond code). No change to the canonical AGI Score or any benchmark data.

v1.10.1 · 2026-06-15 · Full data refresh, plus MiniMax M2.7 (Provisional). A complete re-harvest of every model from independent sources corrected several stale or mislabeled cells (a DeepSeek score that was far too low, a Qwen coding number drawn from the wrong benchmark, and more), filled gaps, and upgraded many cells to higher-trust independent measurements. Effect on the board: the top stays a near-tie between ChatGPT 5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8; Qwen 3.7 Max earns a canonical rank as new coverage completes its profile; Gemini 3 Pro and DeepSeek V4 Pro rise on corrected data. MiniMax M2.7 (the prior MiniMax flagship) joins as Provisional. Every cell traces to an independent source. No imputation.

v1.10.0 · 2026-06-15 · MiniMax M3 added, Ranked at #6. The new MiniMax flagship enters scored entirely from independent sources (Artificial Analysis, vals.ai, benchlm, LiveBench) rather than the lab's own numbers. content_text: v2.0.6 · 2026-07-30 · Our social preview card was still showing pre-v2 numbers, weeks after the numbers changed. Anyone sharing a link to this site saw a card reading 14 live benchmarks, 20 models tracked and “multimodal”. The truth is 10, 21 and Visual Reasoning. The image file on our server was in fact correct and had been regenerated with the rest of the v2 release; what was wrong was our assumption that replacing a file replaces what the world sees. Social platforms cache preview images against the URL, so re-rendering the same filename changes nothing for anyone who has already shared the link, and we had verified the file rather than the card. Every preview image now lives at a versioned URL, the homepage card and all 21 model cards, which forces every platform to fetch it again. The previous files stay where they are, so an existing embed shows an old image rather than a broken one. The card generator carries the version token now, so this is a one-line change next time rather than a rediscovery. This is the same failure as the human-ceiling counts two releases ago: a rendered artifact that nobody re-derived after the thing underneath it changed. The site text was clean, and we checked: no page description, title or preview text anywhere on the site still carries the old figures. v2.0.5 · 2026-07-29 · Tapping a specialty tab on a phone gave you a wall of text instead of scores. The specialty-index notice rendered 586px tall on a 375px screen, 72% of the viewport, and pushed the leaderboard 742px below the tab bar. A reader tapping Coding to see coding scores got a screenful of methodology and had to scroll to find a single number. Below tablet width these notices now collapse to a summary with a More expander, and the full text is one tap away in place. Collapsed, the notice is 151px and the table sits 307px from the tabs, so it is reachable in one short scroll. Nothing was deleted and nothing was softened. The visible summary is a compression, not a gentler version: it still says the specialty index is a 0 to 10 scale rather than the AGI Score, that 10 means a perfect score on every benchmark in the set, and that this is not a human-parity claim. Those are the three things a reader has to know before reading the number, so they stay visible whether or not anybody taps More. The same treatment went to the Value view note about cost being an estimate rather than a measured bill, which kept its estimate caveat in the collapsed line. Switching tabs always re-collapses, so no tab inherits the previous one's expanded state. The expander is a real button with aria-expanded, works without hover, and the Back to AGI Score control stays visible while collapsed. Desktop is unchanged: it has the room, so it shows the full text and no expander at all. v2.0.4 · 2026-07-29 · The mobile tap states would not have rendered on an iPhone. The new section pills carry a pressed state, and it verified correctly in desktop Chromium, which is exactly the wrong place to check it. iOS Safari declines to apply the CSS active state to a link unless a touch listener exists on the element or one of its ancestors, so on the only kind of device that has a touch screen the pills would have looked inert when tapped. One empty listener on the page body fixes it for every tap target on the site. Recorded because verifying a touch behaviour in a mouse browser and calling it done is the kind of shortcut that ships a defect, and because the same trap applies to anything interactive we add from here. v2.0.3 · 2026-07-29 · The site had no mobile navigation at all. On a phone the header rendered a wordmark and a Contribute button and nothing else. The six section links were desktop-only and the version pill was hidden below tablet width, so a visitor on a phone had no route to Corrections, Methodology or anything else, on a page that is otherwise one continuous scroll, and could not see which release they were reading. Small screens now get a compact sticky bar with the version pill visible and a scrolling row of section pills beneath it, carrying the same six anchors as the desktop nav. A row rather than a hamburger: there is no open state to get stuck, nothing to trap keyboard focus, and every section stays one tap away instead of two. Phones also get a back-to-top button once you are far enough down that scrolling back is a chore. Section anchors were landing behind the header at every width, because nothing on the page set a scroll margin; jumping to Corrections put its own heading underneath the sticky bar. Fixed for both layouts. Nothing else moved: the desktop bar is unchanged, and no score, weight or benchmark is touched by this release. v2.0.2 · 2026-07-29 · We were overstating how much of the scale is anchored to humans. Three places on this site claimed that three or four scored benchmarks carry a measured human ceiling, and named OSWorld, FrontierMath and SimpleBench among them. The correct number is one. Of the ten benchmarks on the board, only GPQA Diamond (0.81) carries a measured human ceiling; the other nine are scored against the benchmark maximum, where 100 means a perfect score and no human claim is made at all. The other three did pass the same ceiling audit, and none of them is on the board: OSWorld (0.72) was retired in this very release, and FrontierMath (0.35) and SimpleBench (0.837) have no harvested coverage yet. The claim was wrong in the AGI definition modal, in the methodology summary and in the full methodology, and the three did not even agree with one another. This is the same class of error as the correction we published two versions ago: a number that survived because nobody re-derived it after the thing underneath it changed. The AGI Score is a mixed scale, and it is a good deal more mixed than we were saying. Also in this release: the DeepSeek apology is signed by Barak Laniado, founder and CEO, and its corrections contact is now an email address you can actually write to rather than a link back into the site. The calibration constants box no longer reads “Current as of v1.4” under a v2 banner; the constants are unchanged and were re-confirmed for v2.0.0, which is what it now says. Three hover styles on the corrections card and twelve layout classes on the apology page were also missing from the compiled stylesheet, which is purged to what the leaderboard uses, so they had been failing silently. v2.0.1 · 2026-07-29 · The DeepSeek apology gets its own page. The correction we published in v2.0.0, an ARC-AGI-2 score attributed to DeepSeek V4 Pro that carried no source at all, now has a dedicated page at /corrections/deepseek-arc-agi-2, linked from its entry in the log above. An apology buried as one card among several is easy to walk past, and this one should be readable, citable and linkable on its own. The page sets out what we published, why it was wrong, what it did and did not affect, and what changed in the process so that it cannot recur: under methodology v2 a recorded source is a condition of scoring rather than an expectation, and all 156 scored cells carry one. The wording of the apology itself is unchanged and identical in both places. One count in that entry was also wrong. It said three further cells were voided in the same pass and then referred to four of them in the next sentence. Four further cells were voided, five in total including the DeepSeek one. Corrected here rather than quietly. v2.0.0 · 2026-07-29 · Methodology v2. Every score falls, and no model got worse. Two changes drive it. First, human ceilings. Because a score is normalised as raw divided by a human ceiling, that ceiling is not only an anchor for what counts as human level, it is a volume knob: it multiplies both the level and the spread of a benchmark, and so how hard that benchmark pushes on its component. Most of ours had no measurement behind them. Humanity’s Last Exam sat at 0.50, a number our own internal audit described as a policy floor rather than a finding, and that setting quietly made HLE count double. From now on a ceiling is either a published human result under a protocol comparable to the models’, or it is simply the benchmark maximum and we make no human claim at all. Only four survived the test: GPQA Diamond at 0.81, OSWorld at 0.72 (which we raised, having carried 0.85 against our own recorded measurement), FrontierMath at 0.35, and SimpleBench at 0.837, where we had rounded a human baseline up. Eleven moved to 1.00. Three component scores that previously sat above 100, on a scale whose 100 is meant to be the human mark, no longer do. Second, Agency was rebuilt on four legs across three independent evaluators: SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, τ³-Banking and LiveBench Agentic Coding. Terminal-Bench now comes from vals.ai rather than Artificial Analysis, cutting our reliance on any single evaluator. τ³-Banking enters at benchmark maximum, so its true range shows: the best model completes about a third of these stateful banking workflows. Retired: SWE-bench Pro, OSWorld, BrowseComp, Tau-bench retail and airline, Aider Polyglot, Terminal-Bench 2.0. MCP Atlas demoted to informational. The Tool Use tab is withdrawn until a second clean non-coding benchmark exists. Scores fell by about 6 points from the ceiling change and further from the Agency rebuild; ordering shifted only locally, and the top two are unchanged. Third, evaluator concentration. Artificial Analysis had been supplying 45% of the whole board, 97% of Knowledge and 100% of Visual Reasoning, so one evaluator changing terms would have taken two components to zero. GPQA Diamond and MMMU-Pro moved to vals.ai alongside Terminal-Bench 2.1, taking Artificial Analysis to 26% of the board and splitting Knowledge 52/48 between two evaluators. Every switch was measured before it was made rather than after, and each offset is published rather than absorbed: GPQA Diamond −0.30pp with 1.38pp scatter across all 20 models, MMMU-Pro +5.71pp with 1.67pp scatter and vals higher on all eleven comparable models, Terminal-Bench 2.1 −7.77pp with 4.54pp scatter and vals lower on 18 of 19. One row is held rather than used: vals reports Grok 4.5 at 61.8 on MMMU-Pro, below Grok 4.3 at 83.1 and below xAI’s own non-reasoning variants, which is not a capability measurement we can account for, so we do not use it. Grok 4.5 consequently has no Visual Reasoning cell and falls three places. Visual Reasoning is still single-source, having moved from wholly Artificial Analysis to wholly vals.ai: it rests on one benchmark, so this relocates the dependency rather than removing it, and we would rather say so than imply it is solved. Also in this release: the Reasoning specialty tab is withdrawn. It ran on ARC-AGI-2 and AIME 2025, but AIME 2025 is scored for a single model and sits at 98-99% where it appears, so the tab was ranking on ARC-AGI-2 alone while labelled as using two benchmarks. Withdrawn under the same rule as Tool Use rather than kept with a misleading label; it returns when AIME 2026 is harvested. Cursor Composer 2.5 is removed from the board: it is a product system rather than a model, so under v2 it scores no cells at all, and listing it implied we were waiting on evidence that was never coming. Specialty tabs now report a 0 to 10 index rather than a 0 to 100 score. On the AGI Score, 100 means the genesis of AGI; a specialty score never meant that, and showing both on the same scale implied they were the same kind of claim. Ten now means a perfect score on every benchmark in that set, with no human comparison implied, because most of those benchmarks have no published human study to compare against. The Multimodal component is renamed Visual Reasoning. It rests on a single scored benchmark, MMMU-Pro, which is an exam built on diagrams and charts, so calling 11% of the score “multimodal” claimed a breadth of perception we do not measure. Visual Reasoning says what it is: interpreting image data, which underpins reading a chart, extracting a figure from a document, or working from a screenshot. The AGI definition was revised in the same pass and for the same reason. It previously excluded “sensory perceptions whatsoever”, which contradicted our own scoring of a diagram-based benchmark. Rather than bolt vision on, which would have raised the obvious question of why sight and not hearing or smell, we removed the sensory clause and let the physical-body clause carry the weight: what reaches a model as data is in scope, what needs a body to acquire is not. The definition got shorter. The corrections summary counters have also been replaced. They had been hardcoded since May and one of them read “1 model entered scoring” for two months without meaning anything; they are now derived from the scoring ledger on every release. v1.11.28 · 2026-07-25 · Corrections to our corrections. We audited this log against our own commit history and found that two entries were wrong. Both times we compared two different configurations of the same benchmark and reported the difference as a laboratory overstating its results. DeepSeek did not overstate GPQA Diamond: the 72.9% we published as an independent contradiction is DeepSeek’s own non-thinking-mode figure, reaching us through a secondary aggregator and set against their thinking-mode result. Measured like for like, their self-report sits 1.3 points above independent measurement rather than 17.2 points above. Moonshot did not overstate Humanity’s Last Exam: their 54.0% was explicitly labelled as a with-tools result, and the same post published 36.4% without tools, within half a point of independent measurement. Our source policy had excluded them on the strength of that misreading. Both entries are retracted and both originals are retained rather than deleted. We have also withdrawn a laboratory promotion test that the policy described but that was never run, and corrected an entry which presented source relabelling as new independent measurement. No score, weight, human ceiling or source tier changed in this release. v1.11.27 · 2026-07-25 · Claude Opus 5 and Anthropic roster correction. Added Claude Opus 5 on five independent, variant-distinct frozen-v1 cells: ARC-AGI-2 90.4%, SWE-bench Verified 97.0%, HLE 52.59%, GPQA Diamond 93.23%, and MMMU-Pro 84.74%. The unchanged eligibility engine places it Provisional at 97.31 because one Agency cell and no accepted LiveBench row leave two thin components. The available LiveBench EAP row remains held pending public-model identity resolution; Terminal-Bench 2.1, ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-3 remain outside frozen-v1 scoring. Anthropic’s active latest-two roster is now Opus 5 and Opus 4.8. Fable 5 leaves the current roster under an identity-integrity exception because fallback-enabled, fallback-disabled and generic rows cannot be combined into one standalone model; Opus 4.7 thinking and base retire as older generations. All historical evidence remains preserved, with no transfer or imputation. No formula, weight or source tier changed. v1.11.26 · 2026-07-24 · Grok 4.5 ARC-AGI-2 update. Added ARC Prize’s independently verified Grok 4.5 High result on the 120-task ARC-AGI-2 Public Eval at the official displayed precision of 52.6%. High is the single frozen-v1 scoring configuration; the equal-scoring Medium result and the Low result remain supporting provenance only. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-3 remain informational, and no formula, weight, source tier, roster entry or unrelated evidence changed. No imputation. v1.11.25 · 2026-07-22 · Capability Heatmap isolated from custom weights. The heatmap now reads a separately stored canonical snapshot of default-weight AGI Score, component values, coverage and tier. Explorer sliders and presets continue to recompute AI Score and leaderboard order without changing any heatmap value, order, colour, tooltip or accessible label. This fixes the state-dependent path left open by v1.11.24, whose direct score accessor still pointed to mutable custom-weight state. No score, rank, component, benchmark, evidence, eligibility or methodology changed. No imputation. v1.11.24 · 2026-07-22 · Capability Heatmap AGI Score binding locked. The rightmost heatmap column now declares its full-precision value, colour and accessible label directly from the same canonical final score field used by the leaderboard, model details and Explorer; its default order is explicitly canonical AGI Score descending. blocks.html_en: v2.0.6 · 2026-07-30 · Our social preview card was still showing pre-v2 numbers, weeks after the numbers changed. The image file on our server was in fact correct and had been regenerated with the rest of the v2 release; what was wrong was our assumption that replacing a file replaces what the world sees. Social platforms cache preview images against the URL, so re-rendering the same filename changes nothing for anyone who has already shared the link, and we had verified the file rather than the card. Every preview image now lives at a versioned URL, the homepage card and all 21 model cards, which forces every platform to fetch it again. The previous files stay where they are, so an existing embed shows an old image rather than a broken one. The card generator carries the version token now, so this is a one-line change next time rather than a rediscovery. This is the same failure as the human-ceiling counts two releases ago: a rendered artifact that nobody re-derived after the thing underneath it changed. The site text was clean, and we checked: no page description, title or preview text anywhere on the site still carries the old figures.

blocks.html_en: v2.0.2 · 2026-07-29 · We were overstating how much of the scale is anchored to humans. The claim was wrong in the AGI definition modal, in the methodology summary and in the full methodology, and the three did not even agree with one another. This is the same class of error as the correction we published two versions ago: a number that survived because nobody re-derived it after the thing underneath it changed. The AGI Score is a mixed scale, and it is a good deal more mixed than we were saying. Also in this release: the DeepSeek apology is signed by Barak Laniado, founder and CEO, and its corrections contact is now an email address you can actually write to rather than a link back into the site. The calibration constants box no longer reads “Current as of v1.4” under a v2 banner; the constants are unchanged and were re-confirmed for v2.0.0, which is what it now says. Three hover styles on the corrections card and twelve layout classes on the apology page were also missing from the compiled stylesheet, which is purged to what the leaderboard uses, so they had been failing silently.

blocks.html_en: v2.0.0 · 2026-07-29 · Methodology v2. Every score falls, and no model got worse. Two changes drive it. First, human ceilings. Because a score is normalised as raw divided by a human ceiling, that ceiling is not only an anchor for what counts as human level, it is a volume knob: it multiplies both the level and the spread of a benchmark, and so how hard that benchmark pushes on its component. Most of ours had no measurement behind them. Humanity’s Last Exam sat at 0.50, a number our own internal audit described as a policy floor rather than a finding, and that setting quietly made HLE count double. From now on a ceiling is either a published human result under a protocol comparable to the models’, or it is simply the benchmark maximum and we make no human claim at all. Only four survived the test: GPQA Diamond at 0.81, OSWorld at 0.72 (which we raised, having carried 0.85 against our own recorded measurement), FrontierMath at 0.35, and SimpleBench at 0.837, where we had rounded a human baseline up. Eleven moved to 1.00. Three component scores that previously sat above 100, on a scale whose 100 is meant to be the human mark, no longer do. Second, Agency was rebuilt on four legs across three independent evaluators: SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, τ³-Banking and LiveBench Agentic Coding. Terminal-Bench now comes from vals.ai rather than Artificial Analysis, cutting our reliance on any single evaluator. τ³-Banking enters at benchmark maximum, so its true range shows: the best model completes about a third of these stateful banking workflows. Retired: SWE-bench Pro, OSWorld, BrowseComp, Tau-bench retail and airline, Aider Polyglot, Terminal-Bench 2.0. MCP Atlas demoted to informational. The Tool Use tab is withdrawn until a second clean non-coding benchmark exists. Scores fell by about 6 points from the ceiling change and further from the Agency rebuild; ordering shifted only locally, and the top two are unchanged. Third, evaluator concentration. Artificial Analysis had been supplying 45% of the whole board, 97% of Knowledge and 100% of Visual Reasoning, so one evaluator changing terms would have taken two components to zero. GPQA Diamond and MMMU-Pro moved to vals.ai alongside Terminal-Bench 2.1, taking Artificial Analysis to 26% of the board and splitting Knowledge 52/48 between two evaluators. Every switch was measured before it was made rather than after, and each offset is published rather than absorbed: GPQA Diamond −0.30pp with 1.38pp scatter across all 20 models, MMMU-Pro +5.71pp with 1.67pp scatter and vals higher on all eleven comparable models, Terminal-Bench 2.1 −7.77pp with 4.54pp scatter and vals lower on 18 of 19. One row is held rather than used: vals reports Grok 4.5 at 61.8 on MMMU-Pro, below Grok 4.3 at 83.1 and below xAI’s own non-reasoning variants, which is not a capability measurement we can account for, so we do not use it. Grok 4.5 consequently has no Visual Reasoning cell and falls three places. Visual Reasoning is still single-source, having moved from wholly Artificial Analysis to wholly vals.ai: it rests on one benchmark, so this relocates the dependency rather than removing it, and we would rather say so than imply it is solved. Also in this release: the Reasoning specialty tab is withdrawn. It ran on ARC-AGI-2 and AIME 2025, but AIME 2025 is scored for a single model and sits at 98-99% where it appears, so the tab was ranking on ARC-AGI-2 alone while labelled as using two benchmarks. Withdrawn under the same rule as Tool Use rather than kept with a misleading label; it returns when AIME 2026 is harvested. Cursor Composer 2.5 is removed from the board: it is a product system rather than a model, so under v2 it scores no cells at all, and listing it implied we were waiting on evidence that was never coming. Specialty tabs now report a 0 to 10 index rather than a 0 to 100 score. On the AGI Score, 100 means the genesis of AGI; a specialty score never meant that, and showing both on the same scale implied they were the same kind of claim. Ten now means a perfect score on every benchmark in that set, with no human comparison implied, because most of those benchmarks have no published human study to compare against. The Multimodal component is renamed Visual Reasoning. It rests on a single scored benchmark, MMMU-Pro, which is an exam built on diagrams and charts, so calling 11% of the score “multimodal” claimed a breadth of perception we do not measure. Visual Reasoning says what it is: interpreting image data, which underpins reading a chart, extracting a figure from a document, or working from a screenshot. The AGI definition was revised in the same pass and for the same reason. It previously excluded “sensory perceptions whatsoever”, which contradicted our own scoring of a diagram-based benchmark. Rather than bolt vision on, which would have raised the obvious question of why sight and not hearing or smell, we removed the sensory clause and let the physical-body clause carry the weight: what reaches a model as data is in scope, what needs a body to acquire is not. The definition got shorter. The corrections summary counters have also been replaced. They had been hardcoded since May and one of them read “1 model entered scoring” for two months without meaning anything; they are now derived from the scoring ledger on every release.

sentences.en: v2.0.0 · 2026-07-29 · Methodology v2.
Every score falls, and no model got worse.
sentences.zh: 每个分数都会下降，并且没有模型变得更糟。

sentences.en: Two changes drive it.
sentences.zh: 有两个变化推动了它。

sentences.en: First, human ceilings.
sentences.zh: 首先，人类的天花板。

sentences.en: Because a score is normalised as raw divided by a human ceiling, that ceiling is not only an anchor for what counts as human level, it is a volume knob: it multiplies both the level and the spread of a benchmark, and so how hard that benchmark pushes on its component.
sentences.zh: 因为分数被标准化为原始除以人类上限，所以该上限不仅是人类水平的锚点，而且还是一个音量旋钮：它乘以基准的水平和范围，以及基准对其组件的推动程度。

sentences.en: Most of ours had no measurement behind them.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人的背后都没有衡量标准。

sentences.en: Humanity’s Last Exam sat at 0.50, a number our own internal audit described as a policy floor rather than a finding, and that setting quietly made HLE count double.
sentences.zh: Humanity 的最后一次考试结果为 0.50，我们自己的内部审计将这个数字描述为政策下限，而不是调查结果，而这一设置悄然使 HLE 计数翻倍。

sentences.en: From now on a ceiling is either a published human result under a protocol comparable to the models’, or it is simply the benchmark maximum and we make no human claim at all.
sentences.zh: 从现在开始，上限要么是根据与模型相当的协议发布的人类结果，要么只是基准最大值，我们根本不提出任何人类声明。

sentences.en: Only four survived the test: GPQA Diamond at 0.81, OSWorld at 0.72 (which we raised, having carried 0.85 against our own recorded measurement), FrontierMath at 0.35, and SimpleBench at 0.837, where we had rounded a human baseline up.
sentences.zh: 只有四项通过了测试：GPQA Diamond 为 0.81，OSWorld 为 0.72（我们提高了该值，与我们自己记录的测量相比为 0.85），FrontierMath 为 0.35，SimpleBench 为 0.837，其中我们将人类基线向上舍入。

sentences.en: Eleven moved to 1.00.
Three component scores that previously sat above 100, on a scale whose 100 is meant to be the human mark, no longer do.
sentences.zh: 以前高于 100 分的三个组成部分分数（按 100 分作为人类分数）现在不再如此。

sentences.en: Second, Agency was rebuilt on four legs across three independent evaluators: SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1, τ³-Banking and LiveBench Agentic Coding.
sentences.zh: 其次，Agency 在三个独立评估者的四个方面进行了重建：SWE-bench Verified、Terminal-Bench 2.1、τ³-Banking 和 LiveBench Agentic Coding。

sentences.en: Terminal-Bench now comes from vals.ai rather than Artificial Analysis, cutting our reliance on any single evaluator. τ³-Banking enters at benchmark maximum, so its true range shows: the best model completes about a third of these stateful banking workflows.
sentences.zh: Terminal-Bench 现在来自 vals.ai，而不是人工分析，减少了我们对任何单一评估者的依赖。 τ³-银行业务以基准最大值进入，因此其真实范围表明：最佳模型完成了这些有状态银行工作流程的约三分之一。

sentences.en: Retired: SWE-bench Pro, OSWorld, BrowseComp, Tau-bench retail and airline, Aider Polyglot, Terminal-Bench 2.0.
sentences.zh: 已退役：SWE-bench Pro、OSWorld、BrowseComp、Tau-bench 零售和航空公司、Aider Polyglot、Terminal-Bench 2.0。

sentences.en: Scores fell by about 6 points from the ceiling change and further from the Agency rebuild; ordering shifted only locally, and the top two are unchanged.

sentences.en: Third, evaluator concentration.

sentences.zh: 每个开关都是在进行之前而不是之后进行测量，并且每个偏移都会发布而不是吸收：GPQA Diamond -0.30pp，在所有 20 个模型中具有 1.38pp 散射，MMMU-Pro +5.71pp，在所有 11 个可比模型上具有 1.67pp 散射和较高的值，Terminal-Bench 2.1 -7.77pp，具有 4.54pp 散射，并且在 18 个模型上具有较低的值。 19.

sentences.en: Visual Reasoning is still single-source, having moved from wholly Artificial Analysis to wholly vals.ai: it rests on one benchmark, so this relocates the dependency rather than removing it, and we would rather say so than imply it is solved.

blocks.html_en: v1.11.28 · 2026-07-25 · Corrections to our corrections. We audited this log against our own commit history and found that two entries were wrong. Both times we compared two different configurations of the same benchmark and reported the difference as a laboratory overstating its results. DeepSeek did not overstate GPQA Diamond: the 72.9% we published as an independent contradiction is DeepSeek’s own non-thinking-mode figure, reaching us through a secondary aggregator and set against their thinking-mode result. Measured like for like, their self-report sits 1.3 points above independent measurement rather than 17.2 points above. Moonshot did not overstate Humanity’s Last Exam: their 54.0% was explicitly labelled as a with-tools result, and the same post published 36.4% without tools, within half a point of independent measurement. Our source policy had excluded them on the strength of that misreading. Both entries are retracted and both originals are retained rather than deleted. We have also withdrawn a laboratory promotion test that the policy described but that was never run, and corrected an entry which presented source relabelling as new independent measurement. No score, weight, human ceiling or source tier changed in this release.

blocks.html_en: v1.9.0 · 2026-06-12 · Sensitivity bands on every score, plus a Claude Fable 5 update. Each score on the main leaderboard now shows a sensitivity band (for example 87.02 ±3.6): we remove each of a model's benchmarks one at a time, re-run the entire scoring pipeline, and report how far the score moves. It is not a confidence interval - it shows how much a score depends on which benchmarks exist, and it widens honestly when coverage is thin. When two models' bands overlap, read their order as a statistical tie. Separately, Claude Fable 5 gains its Humanity's Last Exam result from our standardized independent source, lifting its provisional score to about 95.8. It stays Provisional by explicit editorial hold, with the reason published in the open dataset and shown on its badge: ARC-AGI-2 has not yet been run on Fable 5, and every ranked model's reasoning score includes that benchmark, so ranking it today would compare unlike baskets. It ranks the day that result publishes. No imputation, and no corner-cutting in either direction.

v2.0.6 · 2026-07-30 · 在数字更改几周后，我们的社交预览卡仍然显示 v2 之前的数字。 任何分享该网站链接的人都会看到一张卡片，上面写有 14 个实时基准、跟踪的 20 个模型和“多模式”。 事实是 10、21 和视觉推理。 我们服务器上的图像文件实际上是正确的，并且已随 v2 版本的其余部分重新生成；错误的是我们的假设：替换文件就替换了世界所看到的内容。 社交平台根据 URL 缓存预览图像，因此重新呈现相同的文件名对于已经共享链接的任何人来说都不会发生任何变化，而且我们验证的是文件而不是卡片。 现在，每个预览图像都位于版本化 URL、主页卡和所有 21 个模型卡中，这迫使每个平台再次获取它。 以前的文件保留在原来的位置，因此现有的嵌入显示旧图像而不是损坏的图像。 卡生成器现在携带版本令牌，因此下次这是一行更改，而不是重新发现。 这与人类天花板计算两个版本之前的失败相同：渲染的工件在其下面的东西发生变化后没有人重新派生。 网站文本很干净，我们检查过：网站上任何地方都没有页面描述、标题或预览文本仍然带有旧数字。

v2.0.5 · 2026-07-29 · 点击手机上的专业选项卡会给你一堵文字墙而不是分数。 专业索引通知在 375 像素的屏幕上渲染为 586 像素高，占视口的 72%，并将排行榜推到标签栏下方 742 像素。 一位读者点击“编码”来查看编码分数，屏幕上显示了方法论，并且必须滚动才能找到单个数字。 在平板电脑宽度以下，这些通知现在可通过“更多”扩展器折叠为摘要，只需轻轻一按即可就位全文。 折叠后，通知的高度为 151 像素，表格距离选项卡的距离为 307 像素，因此只需一小段滚动即可到达。 没有删除任何内容，也没有软化任何内容。 可见的总结是一个压缩版本，而不是一个更温和的版本：它仍然表示专业指数是 0 到 10 的范围，而不是 AGI 分数，10 意味着集合中每个基准的完美分数，并且这不是人类平等的主张。 这是读者在阅读数字之前必须了解的三件事，因此无论是否有人点击“更多”，它们都保持可见。 同样的处理方式也适用于价值观点注释，即成本是估计而不是测量的账单，这将其估计警告保留在折叠行中。 切换选项卡总是会重新折叠，因此没有选项卡会继承前一个选项卡的展开状态。 扩展器是一个带有 aria 扩展的真实按钮，无需悬停即可工作，并且“返回 AGI 分数”控件在折叠时保持可见。 桌面没有变化：它有空间，所以它显示全文，根本没有扩展器。

v2.0.4 · 2026-07-29 · 移动点击状态不会在 iPhone 上呈现。 新的部分药丸具有压制状态，并且在桌面 Chromium 中验证正确，而这正是检查它的错误位置。 iOS Safari 拒绝将 CSS 活动状态应用于链接，除非该元素或其祖先之一上存在触摸侦听器，因此在唯一一种具有触摸屏的设备上，点击时药丸看起来是惰性的。 页面主体上的一个空侦听器针对网站上的每个点击目标修复了该问题。 记录下来是因为验证鼠标浏览器中的触摸行为并调用它完成是一种会带来缺陷的快捷方式，并且因为相同的陷阱适用于我们从此处添加的任何交互式内容。

v2.0.3 · 2026-07-29 · 该网站根本没有移动导航。 在手机上，标题呈现一个文字标记和一个“贡献”按钮，仅此而已。 这六个部分的链接仅适用于桌面，版本药丸隐藏在平板电脑宽度下方，因此手机上的访问者无法在连续滚动的页面上找到更正、方法论或其他任何内容，并且无法看到他们正在阅读哪个版本。 小屏幕现在有一个紧凑的粘性条，其中版本药丸可见，其下方有一排滚动的部分药丸，带有与桌面导航相同的六个锚点。 一行而不是汉堡：没有打开状态会卡住，没有什么可以捕获键盘焦点，并且每个部分都只需轻按一下而不是两次。 一旦你向下滚动得足够远，向后滚动是一件苦差事，手机也会有一个返回顶部按钮。 部分锚点在每个宽度处都落在标题后面，因为页面上没有任何内容设置滚动边距；跳转到更正将其自己的标题放在粘性栏下方。 两种布局均已修复。 其他没有任何变化：桌面栏没有变化，并且此版本没有触及分数、权重或基准。

v2.0.2 · 2026-07-29 · 我们夸大了人类的规模。 该网站上的三个地方声称三四个得分基准测试具有可测量的人类上限，其中包括 OSWorld、FrontierMath 和 SimpleBench。 正确的数字是一。 在该委员会的十个基准中，只有 GPQA Diamond (0.81) 具有测量的人类上限；另外九个是根据基准最高分数进行评分的，其中 100 意味着满分，并且根本没有人为要求。 其他三个确实通过了相同的上限审核，但没有一个在董事会上：OSWorld (0.72) 在这个版本中已退役，FrontierMath (0.35) 和 SimpleBench (0.837) 尚未收获覆盖范围。 这一主张在 AGI 定义模式、方法论摘要和完整方法论中都是错误的，三者甚至彼此不一致。 这与我们之前发布的两个版本的更正属于同一类错误：这个数字幸存下来，因为在它下面的东西发生变化后没有人重新派生它。 AGI 分数是一个混合量表，而且比我们所说的要混合得多。 此外，在此版本中：DeepSeek 的道歉由创始人兼首席执行官巴拉克·拉尼亚多 (Barak Laniado) 签署，其更正联系人现在是一个您可以实际写入的电子邮件地址，而不是返回该网站的链接。 校准常数框不再在 v2 横幅下显示“当前自 v1.4 起”；常数没有改变，并在 v2.0.0 中重新确认，这就是它现在所说的。 更正卡上的三个悬停样式和道歉页面上的十二个布局类也从编译的样式表中丢失，该样式表被清除为排行榜使用的内容，因此它们一直在默默地失败。

v2.0.1 · 2026-07-29 · DeepSeek 道歉获得了自己的页面。 我们在 v2.0.0 中发布的修正是 DeepSeek V4 Pro 的 ARC-AGI-2 分数，根本没有任何来源，现在有一个专门的页面 / Corrections/deepseek-arc-agi-2，从上面日志中的条目链接。 作为多张卡片中的一张道歉很容易被走过，而且这张卡片本身应该是可读的、可引用的和可链接的。 该页面列出了我们发布的内容、为什么它是错误的、它影响了什么和没有影响什么，以及在过程中发生了什么变化，以便它不会再次发生：在方法论 v2 下，记录的来源是评分条件而不是期望，所有 156 个评分单元格都带有一个。 两处道歉的措辞均未改变且相同。 该条目中的一项计数也是错误的。 它说另外三个牢房在同一次通过中被作废，然后在下一句话中提到了其中的四个。 另外四个单元被作废，包括 DeepSeek 单元在内，总共五个单元。 在这里纠正而不是悄悄地纠正。

v2.0.0 · 2026-07-29 · 方法论 v2.0 每个分数都会下降，并且没有模型变得更糟。 有两个变化推动了它。 首先，人类的天花板。 因为分数被标准化为原始除以人类上限，所以该上限不仅是人类水平的锚点，而且还是一个音量旋钮：它乘以基准的水平和范围，以及基准对其组件的推动程度。 我们大多数人的背后都没有衡量标准。 Humanity 的最后一次考试结果为 0.50，我们自己的内部审计将这个数字描述为政策下限，而不是调查结果，而这一设置悄然使 HLE 计数翻倍。 从现在开始，上限要么是根据与模型相当的协议发布的人类结果，要么只是基准最大值，我们根本不提出任何人类声明。 只有四项通过了测试：GPQA Diamond 为 0.81，OSWorld 为 0.72（我们提高了该值，与我们自己记录的测量相比为 0.85），FrontierMath 为 0.35，SimpleBench 为 0.837，其中我们将人类基线向上舍入。 11 移动到 1.00。 以前高于 100 分的三个组成部分分数（按 100 分作为人类分数）现在不再如此。 其次，Agency 在三个独立评估者的四个方面进行了重建：SWE-bench Verified、Terminal-Bench 2.1、τ³-Banking 和 LiveBench Agentic Coding。 Terminal-Bench 现在来自 vals.ai，而不是人工分析，减少了我们对任何单一评估者的依赖。 τ³-银行业务以基准最大值进入，因此其真实范围表明：最佳模型完成了这些有状态银行工作流程的约三分之一。 已退役：SWE-bench Pro、OSWorld、BrowseComp、Tau-bench 零售和航空公司、Aider Polyglot、Terminal-Bench 2.0。 MCP Atlas 降级为信息性。 工具使用选项卡将被撤回，直到存在第二个干净的非编码基准。 由于上限变化和机构重建，分数下降了约 6 分；排序仅在本地发生变化，前两名没有变化。 第三，评估者的集中度。 人工分析提供了整个棋盘的 45%、97% 的知识和 100% 的视觉推理，因此一个评估者改变术语就会使两个组件为零。 GPQA Diamond 和 MMMU-Pro 与 Terminal-Bench 2.1 一起迁移到 vals.ai，将人工分析占板的 26%，并将 Knowledge 52/48 分配给两个评估者。 每个开关都是在进行之前而不是之后进行测量，并且每个偏移都会发布而不是吸收：GPQA Diamond -0.30pp，在所有 20 个模型中具有 1.38pp 散射，MMMU-Pro +5.71pp，在所有 11 个可比模型上具有 1.67pp 散射和较高的值，Terminal-Bench 2.1 -7.77pp，具有 4.54pp 散射，并且在 18 个模型上具有较低的值。 19. 一行是保留而不是使用：vals 报告 Grok 4.5 在 MMMU-Pro 上的得分为 61.8，低于 Grok 4.3 的得分为 83.1，并且低于 xAI 自己的非推理变体，这不是我们可以解释的能力测量，因此我们不使用它。 因此，Grok 4.5 没有视觉推理单元，排名下降了三位。 视觉推理仍然是单一来源，已经从完全人工分析转向完全 vals.ai：它依赖于一个基准，因此这重新定位了依赖关系而不是删除它，我们宁愿这么说，也不愿暗示它已经解决。 此外，在此版本中：推理专业选项卡已被撤回。 它在 ARC-AGI-2 和 AIME 2025 上运行，但 AIME 2025 是针对单个模型进行评分的，其得分为 98-99%，因此该选项卡仅在 ARC-AGI-2 上排名，同时标记为使用两个基准。 按照与工具使用相同的规则撤回，而不是保留误导性标签；当 AIME 2026 收获时，它就会回归。 Cursor Composer 2.5 已从板上删除：它是一个产品系统，而不是一个模型，因此在 v2 下它根本没有任何单元格得分，列出它意味着我们正在等待永远不会到来的证据。 专业选项卡现在报告 0 到 10 的指数，而不是 0 到 100 的分数。 在AGI评分上，100代表AGI的起源；专业分数从来不意味着这一点，并且以相同的比例显示两者意味着它们是同一类型的主张。 现在，十意味着该组中每个基准的满分，没有暗示人类比较，因为大多数基准没有已发表的人类研究可供比较。 多模式组件更名为视觉推理。 它基于单一评分基准 MMMU-Pro，这是一项基于图表的考试，因此将 11% 的分数称为“多模态”意味着我们无法衡量感知的广度。 视觉推理说明了它的含义：解释图像数据，它支持阅读图表、从文档中提取图形或从屏幕截图进行工作。 AGI 定义在同一过程中出于同样的原因进行了修订。 它之前排除了“任何感官知觉”，这与我们自己对基于图表的基准的评分相矛盾。 我们没有选择视觉，这会提出一个明显的问题，即为什么是视觉而不是听觉或嗅觉，而是删除了感官条款，让物理身体条款承担重量：当数据到达模型时，什么在范围内，而需要身体获取的则不在范围内。 定义变得更短。 更正摘要计数器也已被替换。 它们从 5 月份开始就被硬编码，其中一个在两个月内一直读着“1 个模型进入评分”，但没有任何意义；现在，它们来自每个版本的评分分类帐。

v1.11.28 · 2026-07-25 · 对我们的更正进行更正。 我们根据自己的提交历史记录审核了此日志，发现有两个条目是错误的。 两次我们都比较了同一基准的两种不同配置，并将差异报告为实验室夸大了其结果。 DeepSeek 并没有夸大 GPQA Diamond：我们作为独立矛盾发布的 72.9% 是 DeepSeek 自己的非思维模式数字，通过二级聚合器到达我们并与他们的思维模式结果相对立。 以同样的方式衡量，他们的自我报告比独立测量高出 1.3 个百分点，而不是 17.2 个百分点。 Moonshot 并没有夸大 Humanity 的最后一次考试：他们的 54.0% 被明确标记为使用工具的结果，同一篇文章发布了 36.4% 没有工具的结果，与独立测量相差半个百分点。 由于这种误读，我们的来源政策将他们排除在外。 两个条目都被撤回，并且两个原件都被保留而不是删除。 我们还撤回了政策中描述但从未运行过的实验室升级测试，并更正了将来源重新标记为新的独立测量的条目。 此版本中没有分数、权重、人力上限或来源等级发生变化。

v1.11.27 · 2026-07-25 · Claude Opus 5 和 Anthropic 名册修正。 在五个独立的、变异不同的冷冻 v1 细胞上添加了 Claude Opus 5：ARC-AGI-2 90.4%、SWE-bench Verified 97.0%、HLE 52.59%、GPQA Diamond 93.23% 和 MMMU-Pro 84.74%。 未更改的资格引擎将其暂定为 97.31，因为一个 Agency 单元和没有接受的 LiveBench 行留下了两个薄组件。 可用的 LiveBench EAP 行仍处于等待公共模型身份解析的状态； Terminal-Bench 2.1、ARC-AGI-1 和 ARC-AGI-3 仍处于 freeze-v1 评分之外。 Anthropic 活跃的最新两个名单现在是 Opus 5 和 Opus 4.8。 《神鬼寓言 5》将当前名册置于身份完整性例外之下，因为启用后备、禁用后备和通用行无法合并到一个独立模型中； Opus 4.7 的思维和基础随着老一代的退休。 所有历史证据都得到保存，没有转移或归咎。 配方、重量或来源等级没有改变。

v1.11.26 · 2026-07-24 · Grok 4.5 ARC-AGI-2 更新。 添加了 ARC Priest 独立验证的 Grok 4.5 High 在 120 任务 ARC-AGI-2 Public Eval 上的结果，官方显示精度为 52.6%。 High 是单个 freeze-v1 评分配置；同等得分的“中等”结果和“低”结果仍然仅支持出处。 ARC-AGI-1 和 ARC-AGI-3 仍然是信息性的，公式、重量、来源等级、名册条目或不相关的证据没有改变。 没有归责。

v1.11.25 · 2026-07-22 · 与自定义权重隔离的能力热图。 热图现在读取单独存储的默认权重 AGI 分数、组件值、覆盖范围和层级的规范快照。 资源管理器滑块和预设继续重新计算 AI 分数和排行榜顺序，而不更改任何热图值、顺序、颜色、工具提示或可访问标签。 这修复了 v1.11.24 保持开放的状态相关路径，其直接分数访问器仍然指向可变的自定义权重状态。 分数、等级、组成部分、基准、证据、资格或方法没有改变。 没有归责。

v1.11.24 · 2026-07-22 · 能力热图 AGI 分数绑定已锁定。 最右边的热图列现在直接从排行榜、模型详细信息和资源管理器使用的同一规范最终得分字段声明其全精度值、颜色和可访问标签；它的默认顺序是明确规范的 AGI 分数降序。 无缓存 v1.11.23 预检已呈现规范值，因此此版本不会更改分数、排名、组件、基准、证据、资格或方法。 它添加了机器可验证的绑定合约和针对 Agency 列回归的渲染 DOM 回归覆盖。
